headline: Digital marketing for solar companies in India: the full channel playbook
card_title: Digital marketing for solar companies in India
card_text: What each channel does for a solar EPC, how they fit together, and a 90-day plan to go from scattered enquiries to booked site visits.
intro:
Most solar EPCs in India try digital marketing one channel at a time. They boost a few posts, run Google Ads for a month, or pay someone for SEO, then decide "online doesn't work for solar". The problem is rarely the channel. Solar is a high-ticket, high-trust purchase, and the buyer checks you in several places before letting anyone on their roof.

This guide covers digital marketing for solar companies in India as one system: Google Business Profile, Meta lead ads, Google Search, WhatsApp and SEO. It explains what each channel does, the order to build them in, and how to tell if the system is working. It's based on what we see running campaigns for more than 30 solar EPCs and manufacturers across India.

sections.html:
A homeowner buying rooftop solar is spending a large sum on something they will live with for 25 years. That changes how they shop:

  • Long consideration. Many people watch videos, compare quotes and ask neighbours for weeks before they book a site visit.
  • Trust decides the sale. Reviews, real installation photos and a local address matter more than the lowest price.
  • The subsidy drives interest. Under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, central assistance for homes is currently ₹30,000 for 1 kW, ₹60,000 for 2 kW and ₹78,000 for 3 kW and above. Many enquiries start with "how do I get the subsidy?" Check the current figures on pmsuryaghar.gov.in before you put them in an ad.
  • Two very different buyers. A homeowner in Dwarka and a factory owner in Manesar need different messages, channels and sales processes.

So your marketing has to do two jobs at once: create interest and prove you're trustworthy, quickly, on a phone screen.

The order matters. Build trust first, then switch on paid traffic, and have WhatsApp follow-up ready before the first lead arrives.

sections.h2: Google Business Profile: your shopfront in every search
sections.html:
Before anyone fills your form, they will probably search your company name. Your Google Business Profile is what they see, so get it right before you spend on ads.

  1. Pick the right primary category, such as solar energy company, and add the services you actually offer: rooftop solar for homes, commercial solar, on-grid and hybrid systems.
  2. Add real photos every week: installations, your team on rooftops, inverter setups, happy handovers. Stock images don't build trust.
  3. Ask for a review after every installation. The best moment is handover day, when the system is running and the customer is pleased. Our guide on how to get more Google reviews has a simple system.
  4. Reply to every review, including the bad ones, politely and quickly.
  5. Post updates about the subsidy process, recent installations and seasonal offers.

If you serve several cities, focus your profile and website on the areas you actually cover. Consistent details and fresh reviews help you show up in the map results for those areas.

sections.h2: Meta lead ads: the volume engine
sections.html:
For residential rooftop solar, Facebook and Instagram lead ads are usually the fastest way to get enquiries at scale. Done well, our rooftop solar campaigns run at ₹60–80 per qualified enquiry, and solar clients at scale typically get 20–30 leads a day and 5–10 site visits a week.

Three things separate good solar lead ads from expensive ones:

  • Qualifying questions on the form. Ask whether they own the house, their average monthly electricity bill and their city or pincode. This filters out tenants and people outside your service area before your team calls.
  • Video first. Short videos of real installations, a customer's falling bill or a 30-second subsidy explainer usually hold attention far better than static banners. See our solar ad creative ideas for eight formats to test.
  • New creatives every week. Audiences tire of the same ad quickly. Keep testing hooks and formats so costs don't climb.

Be careful with subsidy claims. Say what the scheme offers and that eligibility depends on the official rules, not "free solar" or "guaranteed subsidy".

sections.h2: Google Search ads: catch people already looking
sections.html:
Meta creates demand. Google Search captures people who have already decided they want solar and are comparing installers. These leads can cost more per enquiry, but the buyer is often further along.

  • Keywords: start with high-intent searches such as "rooftop solar installation", "solar panel for home" with your city name, "solar company near me" and "on-grid solar system price".
  • Negative keywords: exclude "jobs", "course", "training", "dealership" and "wholesale" unless you want those enquiries.
  • Location targeting: target only the cities or pincodes your team can actually serve, set to people located in those areas.
  • Call tracking: many solar buyers prefer to call. Use call assets and track calls as conversions, or you'll undercount what Google is doing.
  • Landing page: send traffic to a page with your installations, reviews, subsidy steps and a short form, not your homepage.

For commercial and industrial solar, Search is often the stronger channel, because factory and warehouse owners search for specific terms like "commercial rooftop solar" or "solar for factory" rather than scrolling Instagram.

sections.h2: WhatsApp: where solar leads are won or lost
sections.html:
The biggest leak we see in solar marketing isn't the ads. It's the gap between a lead arriving and someone replying. A homeowner who fills three installers' forms usually books with the one who responds first and sounds most helpful.

  • Instant auto-reply: send a WhatsApp message within a minute with a short introduction, a real installation video and a link to book a site visit.
  • Collect details in the chat: roof type, monthly bill, sanctioned load and location, so your sales team calls with context.
  • Follow-up sequence: day 1, day 3 and day 7 messages with a customer story, the subsidy steps and an offer to visit.
  • Click-to-WhatsApp ads: let people start the conversation directly from a Meta ad. This works well for buyers who don't want to fill forms.

WhatsApp Business Platform pricing is set per message and by category, and Meta has changed the rules several times, including in 2026. Check the current rates for India before you plan large broadcasts, and only message people who have opted in. Our WhatsApp automation service sets these flows up end to end.

sections.h2: SEO and content: the channel that compounds
sections.html:
SEO is slower, usually three to six months before it brings steady enquiries, but those enquiries don't stop when your ad budget does. For a solar company, the pages that tend to earn traffic are practical ones:

  • City or area pages for every location you serve
  • A clear subsidy guide: who is eligible, the steps, and how long it takes
  • Price guides by system size, with honest ranges and what changes them
  • Project pages with photos, system size and the customer's area

Keep the website fast on mobile, put your phone number and WhatsApp button on every page, and make sure your business name, address and phone match your Google Business Profile.

sections.h2: A 90-day plan for a solar EPC
sections.html:
1. Weeks 1–2: fix your Google Business Profile, collect reviews from recent customers, set up tracking for forms, calls and WhatsApp clicks, and build one landing page.
  2. Weeks 3–6: launch Meta lead ads with qualifying questions and five to ten creatives, switch on WhatsApp auto-replies, and start Google Search on your highest-intent keywords.
  3. Weeks 7–12: cut ads and keywords that don't produce site visits, scale the ones that do, add retargeting, and publish your first city and subsidy pages.

Measure cost per site visit and cost per installation, not just cost per lead. A cheap lead that never answers the phone is the most expensive kind. For a step-by-step version focused on Delhi NCR, read how to get solar leads in Delhi NCR, or see how we've done this in our solar case studies.

faqs: What is the best digital marketing channel for solar companies in India?

There isn't one best channel. For residential rooftop solar, Meta lead ads usually bring the most enquiries, Google Search brings buyers who are already comparing installers, and Google reviews and WhatsApp follow-up decide how many of those enquiries become site visits. Most EPCs get the best results by running them together.
How much does a solar lead cost in India?

It depends on your city, offer, creatives and how strictly you qualify leads. Our rooftop solar campaigns run at ₹60–80 per qualified enquiry. Judge cost per site visit and cost per installation, not just cost per lead.
Can solar companies mention the PM Surya Ghar subsidy in ads?

Yes, as long as the claim is accurate. State what the scheme currently offers, link to or mention the official portal, and make clear that eligibility depends on the scheme rules. Avoid phrases like "free solar" or "guaranteed subsidy", and check the current figures before every campaign.
How long does digital marketing take to work for a solar business?

Paid ads on Meta and Google can bring enquiries within the first week or two. Getting to a steady, profitable cost per installation usually takes 30 to 90 days of testing. SEO and Google Business Profile rankings typically take three to six months.
Should commercial solar be marketed differently from rooftop solar for homes?

Yes. Commercial and industrial buyers search for specific terms and care about payback, power bills and reliability, so Google Search, a strong website with project details and direct outreach usually work better than Instagram ads aimed at homeowners.
